page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.large is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance within the ecs.sn1 server family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and relies on a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor provides a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. Supported hardware instruction sets include AVX, AVX512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, though newer extensions such as AVX512_VNNI and AMX are absent. In synthetic CPU benchmarks, the instance demonstrates performance in the bottom 25% tier, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1103.98 and a multi-core score of 2930.09. PassMark CPU testing yields a score of 3617.68, placing its raw computational capabilities in the lower performance bracket.

Memory performance is constrained, with PassMark memory testing scoring in the bottom 10% at 1241.98. Read-only memory bandwidth for large blocks is measured at 20.95 GB/sec, while write bandwidth for large blocks reaches 18.75 GB/sec. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached volumes, which must share the baseline 1 Gbps network interface. This network limitation also impacts web serving throughput, which registers at 2.42 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is structured for compute-oriented workloads that do not require large memory footprints. Benchmark results indicate weak performance across database operations (1099.9 on PassMark) and text processing (1179.0 on Geekbench). Redis SET operations reach 2.79 million operations per second, and small-model LLM inference (135M) achieves 60.86 tokens per second for text generation. The instance is suited for lightweight utility computing, basic web serving, or development environments where dedicated CPU cores are required without demanding high-throughput memory or storage performance.
